v: One of the scribes came, and heard them questioning together, and knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”
Jesus answered, “The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one:
you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
The second is like this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
The scribe said to him, “Truly, teacher, you have said well that he is one, and there is none other but he,

and to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from God’s Kingdom.” No one dared ask him any question after that.
b: This passage records a profound conversation in which Jesus was asked which commandment is the most important. The question came from a scribe, and Jesus' answer summed up the heart of the whole Law: love God and love people. Jesus first quoted Deuteronomy, stressing that the Lord is the only God and that we should love him with all our heart. Second, he said we should love our neighbor as ourselves. These two commandments are closely bound together and form the foundation of the life of faith.

Jesus' answer not only made clear the priorities of the Law but also revealed the link between worship and ethics. Love for God cannot stop at religious ritual or inner devotion; it must be expressed concretely by loving our neighbor as ourselves. Such love is unconditional and all-embracing, reaching not only family and friends but also those we do not know, and even those who may be hostile to us.

When the scribe agreed with Jesus' answer, Jesus commended his wisdom and told him he was not far from the kingdom of God. This shows that understanding and accepting these two commandments is an important step toward God's kingdom. Through this passage God reminds us that the practice of faith is not merely a matter of form, but must be truly embodied in our love for God and for others.
q: How do you express your love for God and for others in daily life? What concrete actions could help you better practice these two greatest commandments?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us the commandment to love you and the commandment to love others. Give us strength to love you with all our hearts in daily life and to love those around us in practical ways. May our lives reflect your unconditional love and keep growing in love. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple, “How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
For David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.” ’
Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?” The common people heard him gladly.
b: In this passage Jesus quotes David's psalm to challenge the teaching of the religious leaders of his day. He points out that David called the Christ "Lord," which shows that the Christ is not only David's descendant but David's Lord. This means the Christ is not merely a human king but the divine ruler. Jesus' question reveals the Christ's two natures: he is both man and God.

This passage invites us to think about the true identity of Christ. He is not an ordinary king, but the Son of God, who holds authority above all. Understanding and acknowledging this is vital to our faith. It reminds us that Jesus Christ is not only our Savior but also the Lord of our lives, and deserves our wholehearted worship and obedience.

Through this passage God tells us that knowing the true identity of Jesus Christ is of utmost importance. He is the promised Messiah and the Lord of each one of our lives. We should honor him in our daily living and let him be the center of all our decisions and actions.
q: How do you show honor and obedience to Jesus Christ in your life? What concrete ways could help you know him better and acknowledge him as your Lord?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for revealing the true identity of Jesus Christ. Help us to honor him as Lord every day and to follow his leading with all our hearts in our lives. May our lives glorify your name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury, and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.
A poor widow came, and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.
He called his disciples to himself, and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,
for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”
b: This passage describes Jesus watching people give their offerings in the temple, and the most striking was the poor widow's gift. Although her offering was tiny, Jesus praised it as more than that of all the rich, because she gave everything she had. It is a thought-provoking story that teaches us that the true meaning of giving lies not in the size of the amount but in the heart and motive with which we give.

Jesus' teaching helps us see that true giving is an act of love and faith, a complete entrusting of ourselves. When we give, what God values is whether our hearts belong wholly to him, not how much we can give. The widow's gift was praised because she held nothing back and placed herself in God's hands. This is an expression of faith worth learning for every believer.

Through this passage God tells us that giving is not only a matter of material things, but an expression of our complete trust in God. However much we have, what matters is that we are willing to give ourselves to God without reserve and let him rule our lives.
q: How do you show complete trust in God in daily life? What concrete acts of giving could help you express your love and reverence for God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us the true meaning of giving. Help us to follow the widow's example and be willing to give you everything we have without reserve. However much we have, may our hearts belong wholly to you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: As he went out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings!”
Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here one stone on another, which will not be thrown down.”
b: This passage describes a conversation between Jesus and his disciples at the temple. The disciples marveled at the magnificent buildings, but Jesus prophesied that these great buildings would be torn down. This prophecy was undoubtedly shocking to the disciples, because the temple held an extremely important place and symbolic meaning in their faith. Yet Jesus' words reveal a deeper truth: the things of earth are all temporary, and only God's kingdom is eternal.

Jesus' prophecy should make us reflect on whether we depend too much on and value too highly the achievements and wealth of this world, while neglecting spiritual things. Earthly glory and achievements will pass away, and only God's kingdom cannot be shaken. So we should fix our attention on heavenly things and pursue spiritual wealth that never decays.

Through this passage God tells us that we should rise above our infatuation with earthly things and set our eyes on the things of the kingdom of heaven. Only God's kingdom is our eternal home, and we should strive for the spiritual wealth that can never be destroyed.
q: How can you rise above infatuation with possessions and achievements in daily life and focus on pursuing spiritual wealth? What concrete actions could help you readjust your focus?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us that earthly things are temporary. Help us not to be deceived by possessions and achievements, but to fix our eyes on your eternal kingdom. May our hearts always long for spiritual things, and may we live lives worthy of your kingdom. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,
“Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are all about to be fulfilled?”
Jesus, answering, began to tell them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he!’ and will lead many astray.
“When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines and troubles. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
But watch yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils. You will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them.
The Good News must first be preached to all the nations.

When they lead you away and deliver you up, don’t be anxious beforehand, or premeditate what you will say, but say whatever will be given you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
“Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.
b: In this passage Jesus foretells the signs and troubles that will come at the end of the age. He tells his disciples that many will come in his name, claiming to be the Christ, and will cause widespread confusion and disaster. Jesus warns his disciples to stay alert and not be deceived, and tells them that these troubles are only the beginning, and the real challenges are yet to come.

Jesus foretells that believers will face persecution and even betrayal by family members, all for his name's sake. This helps us see that following Christ is not easy but takes courage and perseverance. He reminds us that the gospel must be preached to all nations, and that when believers are put on trial and persecuted they need not worry, because the Holy Spirit will give us wisdom and words so that we can bear witness for the Lord.

Through this passage God tells us that the end times will be full of challenges and trials, but believers must hold fast to faith and rely on the power of the Holy Spirit to face these difficulties. Those who endure to the end will be saved. We must be ready at all times to meet the Lord's return with faith and patience.
q: How do you prepare yourself to face the challenges of the end times? In what areas do you need to rely more on the Holy Spirit's guidance and strength?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us through Jesus Christ's prophecy of the challenges of the end times. Give us faith and courage so that in difficulties we hold firmly to our faith and rely on the Holy Spirit's power to bear witness. May our lives reflect our loyalty to you and our hope in you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not” (let the reader understand), “then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains,
and let him who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.
Let him who is in the field not return back to take his cloak.
But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse babies in those days!
Pray that your flight won’t be in the winter.
For in those days there will be oppression, such as there has not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will be.
Unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he picked out, he shortened the days.
Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ don’t believe it.
For there will arise false christs and false prophets, and will show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
But you watch. “Behold, I have told you all things beforehand.
b: In this passage Jesus describes to his disciples further the troubles of the end times, especially the scene when "the abomination of desolation" appears in the holy place. Jesus warns that when these things happen, believers should flee at once, because a tribulation unequaled before will come. These troubles will be so severe that, for the sake of the elect, God must shorten those days, or no one would be saved.

This passage also warns us that in the end times false christs and false prophets will appear and may even deceive the elect. So believers must stay alert and not readily believe any claim to be the Christ, but keep in mind Jesus' teaching and warnings.

Through this passage God tells us that the coming of the end times will bring great tests and challenges, but God's protection of his elect is certain. In such an age we need to keep faith and stay alert, holding closely to God's guidance so that we are not misled.
q: How do you stay alert when facing deception and temptation? What practical ways could help you rely on God's guidance in daily life and walk the right path?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us through Jesus Christ of the challenges of the end times. Help us, when we face difficulties and temptations, to stay alert and keep faith, and to walk the right path by your guidance. May we show your glory through these trials. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: But in those days, after that oppression, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light,
the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
Then he will send out his angels, and will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the sky.
b: This passage portrays the extreme scenes of the end of the age: when the order of nature is disturbed, the sun and moon are darkened, the stars fall, and the powers in the heavens are shaken, the Son of Man will appear in glory and send out his angels to gather his elect. This scene not only foreshadows the severe challenges of the end times but also shows the return of Jesus Christ and God's ultimate victory.

This passage reminds us that however frightening the scenes of the end times, for God's elect they are also part of God's plan of redemption. The Son of Man's return will bring righteous judgment and will save his elect. We should wait for that day with faith and hope, because we know that however circumstances change, God's promises never change.

Through this passage God tells us that we need not fear the disasters of the end times, because God's salvation and promises are certain. We should welcome the return of the Son of Man with faith, and keep watchful and godly lives while we wait.
q: How do you keep expectation and hope for the return of the Son of Man in daily life? What practical ways could help you live a godly life during this time of waiting?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us hope and strength through Jesus Christ's prophecy. Help us to keep faith as we face future challenges, waiting for the return of the Son of Man. May our lives in the meantime reflect our loyalty to you and reverence for you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: “Now from the fig tree, learn this parable. When the branch has now become tender, and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near;
even so you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.
Most certainly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
b: In this passage Jesus uses the fig tree as a parable to teach his disciples how to recognize the signs of the end of the age. When the fig tree's branch becomes tender and puts out its leaves, people know that summer is near; in the same way, when the disciples see the signs of the end, they should know that the return of the Son of Man is at the door. Jesus stresses that his prophecy is certain and his words will surely come to pass; even if heaven and earth pass away, his words will not change.

This passage teaches us to heed God's word and stay alert in life. Although we cannot know the exact time of the Lord's return, we should learn from the signs and changes in life and be ready to meet him. This means living at all times within God's will, following his word, and waiting for that day in faith.

Through this passage God tells us that his words never change and his promises will surely be fulfilled. We should hold on in faith and look forward to his return with reverence, letting our lives reflect trust in and obedience to God's word.
q: How do you heed God's word in daily life and prepare for the Lord's return? What concrete actions could help you persevere in faith?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us through Jesus Christ to stay alert and be prepared. Help us to follow your word at all times and to look forward to the Lord's return in faith. May our lives reflect firm trust in your word. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: But of that day or that hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you don’t know when the time is.
“It is like a man, traveling to another country, having left his house, and given authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and also commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.
Watch therefore, for you don’t know when the lord of the house is coming, whether at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning;
lest coming suddenly he might find you sleeping.
What I tell you, I tell all: Watch.”
b: In this passage Jesus reminds us to stay alert at all times, because no one knows the time of the Lord's return, not even the angels in heaven or the Son, but only the Father. So we should be like the doorkeeper, ready at any moment for the master of the house to return. Jesus uses a parable to tell us that, whenever and wherever we are, we must keep spiritually alert and not fall into spiritual sleep, because the Lord may come at any time.

This passage warns us not to become slack or careless because we are unsure when the Lord will return, but to faithfully complete the work God has entrusted to us each day and stay alert in spirit. We need to watch and pray, seeking God's guidance and strength, and be ready to meet the Lord. In this way, even if the Lord comes suddenly, we can face him with confidence and without fear.

Through this passage God tells us to stay alert every day and be ready for the Lord's return. Watchfulness is not only outward preparation but an inner alertness of heart. We should pray often, draw near to God, and live within his will.
q: In your daily life, how do you keep spiritually alert and prepare for the Lord's return? What concrete actions could help you stay watchful in spirit?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us to stay alert at all times and prepare for the Lord's return. Help us to serve you faithfully every day and not let spiritual slackness enter our lives. May we watch and pray often, stay close to you, and be ready to meet you when you come again. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: It was now two days before the feast of the Passover and the unleavened bread, and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might seize him by deception, and kill him.
For they said, “Not during the feast, because there might be a riot among the people.”

While he was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at the table, a woman came having an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard—very costly. She broke the jar, and poured it over his head.
But there were some who were indignant among themselves, saying, “Why has this ointment been wasted?
For this might have been sold for more than three hundred denarii,  and given to the poor.” So they grumbled against her.
But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for me.
For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want to, you can do them good; but you will not always have me.
She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for the burying.
Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News may be preached throughout the whole world, that which this woman has done will also be spoken of for a memorial of her.”
b: This passage describes an event in Bethany in which a woman anointed Jesus' head with very costly pure nard ointment. This act upset some of those present, who considered it a waste, since the ointment could have been sold and the money given to the poor. But Jesus praised the woman's deed, pointing out that she was preparing his body for burial.

This passage shows us that love and devotion to Jesus surpass everything. Although this woman's action was misunderstood and criticized, her intention was fully understood and accepted by Jesus. Jesus even said that wherever the gospel is preached, what she did would be remembered. This reminds us that our devotion to God should not waver because of others' misunderstanding, since God looks at the heart.

Through this passage God tells us that love and devotion to him should be without counting the cost. We should learn from this woman's example and give our best to God, even if the world may not understand or accept it. For in God's eyes, true giving is a response of love, not a calculation of gain and loss.
q: How do you show wholehearted devotion to God in life? What concrete actions could help you better give your best to God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us how to offer our love and devotion wholeheartedly. Help us not to be swayed by the opinions of the world, but to keep giving our best to you. May all our actions glorify your name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests, that he might deliver him to them.
They, when they heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. He sought how he might conveniently deliver him.
b: This passage is short but deeply significant, describing Judas' decision to betray Jesus. He made an agreement with the chief priests, willing to betray Jesus for the sake of silver. It is a heartbreaking scene in the Gospels, showing the weakness and sin of the human heart.

This passage reminds us that however close we are to Jesus, and however much we may seem outwardly to be his disciples, the motives and intentions of our hearts are crucial to our actions. Judas seemed to have followed Jesus for years, yet his heart was ruled by greed and betrayal, and in the end he chose to sell Jesus. We need to examine our hearts regularly to make sure our faith is genuine and not shaken by worldly gain and temptation.

Through this passage God tells us that faith is not outward following but inner loyalty. We must take care that worldly temptations do not affect our love and loyalty to Christ, and we should often ask God to cleanse our hearts.
q: Have you faced inner temptation and worldly enticement? How can you stay loyal to God and keep your faith pure in such situations?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for warning us to guard against temptation and sin in our hearts. Help us to keep our hearts pure and not be deceived by worldly gain. May our faith stand firm in every circumstance and stay loyal to you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: On the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, his disciples asked him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare that you may eat the Passover?”
He sent two of his disciples, and said to them, “Go into the city, and there you will meet a man carrying a pitcher of water. Follow him,
and wherever he enters in, tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?” ’
He will himself show you a large upper room furnished and ready. Get ready for us there.”
His disciples went out, and came into the city, and found things as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
b: This passage describes how Jesus and his disciples prepared the Passover meal. Jesus arranged everything in advance and gave the disciples detailed instructions on how to find the place. The disciples trusted Jesus completely and followed his directions, and in the end found the room as appointed and prepared the Passover meal.

This passage shows us Jesus' command of the future and his all-knowing power. He knew clearly all that was about to happen and had already arranged everything for his disciples. We can learn from this that whatever situation we face, if we follow Jesus' guidance, he will open the way for us and make everything go smoothly.

Through this passage God tells us that we should trust Jesus' guidance with all our hearts, because he has already prepared everything. Even if we cannot see the road ahead, if we follow in his steps, he will lead us to the right destination.
q: Do you often feel lost or uncertain in life? How can you learn to trust Jesus' guidance and believe that he has prepared the road ahead for you?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for showing us through Jesus Christ your command and arrangement of our lives. Give us faith to trust your guidance completely and to walk in the path you have prepared. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: When it was evening he came with the twelve.
As they sat and were eating, Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, one of you will betray me—he who eats with me.”
They began to be sorrowful, and to ask him one by one, “Surely not I?” And another said, “Surely not I?”
He answered them, “It is one of the twelve, he who dips with me in the dish.
For the Son of Man goes, even as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
b: This passage records the conversation between Jesus and his disciples at the Last Supper, in which he foretold that his betrayer would be among the disciples. This prophecy shocked and troubled the disciples, and one by one they asked Jesus whether he meant them. Jesus did not name him directly, but hinted at the identity of the disciple who would betray him.

This passage reminds us that Jesus knows everything that will happen: he knows who will betray him and who will stay loyal. The event also highlights the frailty of the human heart: even someone who has followed Jesus for years may fall through temptation and weakness. So we should stay alert at all times, guard our hearts, and avoid being lured by sin.

Through this passage God tells us that however close we are to Jesus, we need to humble ourselves and be on guard against temptation in our hearts. Only by relying on God's grace can we persevere on the path of faith and not be led astray by sin.
q: Have you felt temptation from within or without? How can you rely on God's grace to resist these temptations and stay on the path of faith?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for helping us understand the weakness of the human heart and the reality of temptation. Help us to stay alert at all times and guard our hearts against the allure of sin. May we persevere to the end on the path of faith, loyal to you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, and when he had blessed, he broke it, and gave to them, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body.”
He took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them. They all drank of it.
He said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.
Most certainly I tell you, I will no more drink of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it anew in God’s Kingdom.”
b: This passage records Jesus' institution of the Lord's Supper. He gave the bread and the cup to his disciples, telling them that these symbolize his body and blood, and foretelling that he was about to give himself for the sins of the world. This is an extremely important moment in the Christian faith, and the Lord's Supper has become the sign by which believers remember the Lord's sacrifice and share in his life.

This passage reminds us that the Lord's Supper is not only a ritual of remembrance but also a sign of our union with Christ. Each time we receive the Lord's Supper, we reaffirm our faith in Christ and take part in his suffering and resurrection. It makes us aware of how deep Christ's love is: he was willing to lay down his life for us and establish a new covenant for us, so that we could be reconciled to God.

Through this passage God tells us that the sacrifice of Jesus Christ is the foundation of our salvation. We should receive the Lord's Supper with thankful hearts, remember all he has done for us, and be willing to share in his life.
q: How do you deeply remember and experience Christ's love when you receive the Lord's Supper? How does this affect your life of faith?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving your beloved Son Jesus Christ to lay down his life for our sins. Help us, when we receive the Lord's Supper, to grasp its meaning deeply and to remember the Lord's sacrifice with grateful hearts. May our lives be changed by his love. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
However, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”
But Peter said to him, “Although all will be offended, yet I will not.”
Jesus said to him, “Most certainly I tell you, that you today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
But he spoke all the more, “If I must die with you, I will not deny you.” They all said the same thing.
b: This passage records Jesus foretelling that the disciples would be scattered when he suffered, and in particular that Peter would deny him three times before the rooster crowed twice. Peter strongly objected, saying that even if he had to die with Jesus, he would not deny him. But Jesus knew clearly Peter's weakness and what was to come.

This passage reminds us that however firm we think we are, we may fall before temptation and pressure. Peter's example shows that even the most loyal disciple may fail at a critical moment. We need to humble ourselves, admit our weakness, and rely on God's strength to hold to our faith.

Through this passage God tells us not to be overconfident, thinking we can hold on to our faith by our own strength. We should rely on God's grace and stay alert at all times, because only with God's help can we overcome temptation and challenge.
q: When you face temptation and challenge, have you felt that you might be weak? How can you rely on God's strength to keep your faith firm?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us not to be overconfident but to rely humbly on your strength. Help us to hold fast to our faith under temptation and pressure and not turn away from your way. May we rely on your grace in every challenge and remain loyal to you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: They came to a place which was named Gethsemane. He said to his disciples, “Sit here, while I pray.”
He took with him Peter, James, and John, and began to be greatly troubled and distressed.
He said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here, and watch.”
He went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.
He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Couldn’t you watch one hour?
Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again he went away, and prayed, saying the same words.
Again he returned, and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy, and they didn’t know what to answer him.
He came the third time, and said to them, “Sleep on now, and take your rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Arise! Let’s get going. Behold: he who betrays me is at hand.”
b: This passage records Jesus' anguished prayer in the Garden of Gethsemane. He knew well the suffering he was about to face, and his soul was very sorrowful, even to death. Yet he was still willing to submit to the Father's will and face the cross that was coming. The disciples, however, fell asleep at such a moment and could not watch and pray with him.

This passage reminds us that even in great pain and temptation, Jesus still chose to submit to God's will, an example we should follow. The disciples' weakness also warns us how important it is to watch and pray, because our flesh often leads us into weakness and slackness at critical moments.

Through this passage God tells us that when we face temptation and suffering, we should be like Jesus, persisting in prayer and seeking God's will. Even when our hearts are in unbearable pain, we should still trust God and submit to his leading, because his plan is far beyond our understanding.
q: Have you felt helpless when facing difficulty? How can you persist in prayer at such times, seek God's will, and submit to his leading?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see Jesus' submission to and trust in you in his suffering. Help us, when we face temptation and difficulty, to persist in prayer and rely on your strength. May our hearts stay alert and not fall into weakness and slackness. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: Immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, came—and with him a multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
Now he who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “Whomever I will kiss, that is he. Seize him, and lead him away safely.”
When he had come, immediately he came to him, and said, “Rabbi! Rabbi!” and kissed him.
They laid their hands on him, and seized him.
But a certain one of those who stood by drew his sword, and struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
Jesus answered them, “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs to seize me?
I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me. But this is so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled.”
They all left him, and fled.
b: This passage describes the scene in Gethsemane where Jesus was betrayed by Judas and arrested. Judas used a kiss as a signal and betrayed Jesus, and so he was seized. When the disciples saw Jesus arrested, they all fled, leaving Jesus alone to face the suffering that was coming.

This passage reminds us that even at the moment of betrayal and arrest, Jesus still showed composure and firmness. He did not resist, because he knew this was God's plan, for accomplishing salvation. In contrast to the disciples' flight, Jesus' conduct shows his complete submission to God's will.

Through this passage God tells us that even when we face betrayal and difficulty, we should be like Jesus, keeping faith, relying on God's leading, and carrying out his will. We should learn Jesus' obedience and courage, and hold on to our faith even in adversity.
q: When you face betrayal or difficulty, are you able to keep trusting God as Jesus did? How can you seek his strength and guidance at such times?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, who set us an example of obedience and courage. Help us, when we face betrayal and difficulty, to keep trusting you and to submit to your will. May we witness your power and grace in every challenge. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: A certain young man followed him, having a linen cloth thrown around himself over his naked body. The young men grabbed him,
but he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.
b: This passage records a detail that seems unimportant but is rich in symbolism. This young man may symbolize those followers who fled in fear. They had meant to follow Jesus, but when faced with danger chose to run away, even leaving everything behind to save their lives.

This passage reminds us that following Jesus is not only a verbal commitment but also takes perseverance in difficulty and challenge. We may want to run away out of fear or unease, but a true believer should keep following Jesus in every circumstance, whatever the cost.

Through this passage God tells us that the path of faith is not easy, but we should follow Jesus without letting up, and not shrink back even in the face of difficulty and danger. We should learn to rely on God's strength and persevere in walking in his will.
q: On your journey of faith, have you felt afraid or wanted to run away? How can you rely on God's strength to keep going when you face challenges?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us through this passage of the challenges and cost of faith. Give us courage to keep following Jesus firmly when we face difficulty, without running away or shrinking back. May our whole lives walk in your will. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: They led Jesus away to the high priest. All the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes came together with him.
Peter had followed him from a distance, until he came into the court of the high priest. He was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of the fire.
Now the chief priests and the whole council sought witnesses against Jesus to put him to death, and found none.
For many gave false testimony against him, and their testimony didn’t agree with each other.
Some stood up, and gave false testimony against him, saying,
“We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I will build another made without hands.’ ”
Even so, their testimony didn’t agree.
The high priest stood up in the middle, and asked Jesus, “Have you no answer? What is it which these testify against you?”
But he stayed quiet, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?”
Jesus said, “I am. You will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of the sky.”
The high priest tore his clothes, and said, “What further need have we of witnesses?
You have heard the blasphemy! What do you think?” They all condemned him to be worthy of death.
Some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to beat him with fists, and to tell him, “Prophesy!” The officers struck him with the palms of their hands.
b: This passage records the trial of Jesus before the high priest. He faced false witnesses and unjust accusations, yet remained silent, until he himself confirmed his identity: the Son of God, the Christ. This declaration led the high priest and the council to decide to condemn him.

This passage reminds us that in the face of great injustice and false accusation, Jesus still chose to endure and to submit to God's will. What courage and faith that was! He did not defend himself but firmly accepted the fate of the cross, because he knew it was to fulfill God's plan of salvation.

Through this passage God tells us that faith is not only perseverance in good times but also endurance and trust in adversity. When we face injustice or misunderstanding, we should learn from Jesus' example, rely on God's strength, hold to the truth, and trust his final judgment.
q: Have you ever felt injustice or misunderstanding in your life? How can you keep your faith and rely on God's strength to face it?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for showing us through Jesus Christ how to hold to our faith and submit to your will in the face of injustice and misunderstanding. Give us strength so that in difficulties we may rely on you, hold to the truth, and not be shaken by worldly pressure. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: As Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the maids of the high priest came,
and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him, and said, “You were also with the Nazarene, Jesus!”
But he denied it, saying, “I neither know, nor understand what you are saying.” He went out on the porch, and the rooster crowed.
The maid saw him, and began again to tell those who stood by, “This is one of them.”
But he again denied it. After a little while again those who stood by said to Peter, “You truly are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech shows it.”
But he began to curse, and to swear, “I don’t know this man of whom you speak!”
The rooster crowed the second time. Peter remembered the word, how that Jesus said to him, “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” When he thought about that, he wept.
b: This passage tells of Peter's three denials of the Lord during Jesus' trial. Although Peter had earlier firmly declared that he would not deny Jesus, under pressure and fear he in the end denied three times any relationship with Jesus. When the rooster crowed, Peter remembered Jesus' prophecy and was deeply grieved over his weakness.

This passage lets us see that even the most loyal disciple may fall into weakness under pressure and deny his faith. But Peter's remorse and repentance also tell us that God is full of mercy, and if we truly repent he will forgive our transgressions. This reminds us to stay humble at all times and rely on God's strength, not our own, to hold on to our faith.

Through this passage God tells us that we need to stay alert at all times and avoid denying the Lord under temptation and pressure. When we are weak, we should not fall into despair, but truly repent and seek God's forgiveness and restoration.
q: When facing challenges to your faith, have you felt fear or weakness? How can you rely on God's strength to persevere in such situations?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see Peter's example, which reminds us to stay alert in temptation. Help us to rely on your strength under pressure and difficulty and not deny our faith. If we fall, help us to repent sincerely and return to your arms. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

v: Immediately in the morning the chief priests, with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation, bound Jesus, carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.
Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” He answered, “So you say.”
The chief priests accused him of many things.
Pilate again asked him, “Have you no answer? See how many things they testify against you!”
But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate marveled.
b: This passage describes how Jesus, after the religious leaders' accusations, was brought before the Roman governor Pilate to stand trial. After consulting together, the leaders bound Jesus and handed him over to Pilate, which reveals both their hostility toward Jesus and their attempt to use Roman power to be rid of him. Pilate asked Jesus whether he was "the King of the Jews." The question was political and dangerous, yet Jesus' answer was extremely brief and did not directly challenge Pilate's authority.

Faced with so many accusations, Jesus chose to remain silent. His silence was obedience to God's will, and it was also his steadfast endurance under extreme pressure. Jesus did not defend himself but chose to trust God's plan. Pilate marveled at his silence, which shows that Jesus' response was entirely different from that of the prisoners Pilate had seen before when they faced the threat of death. Jesus' bearing reflects his inner peace and his complete trust in God.

This passage reminds us that when we face unjust accusations or misunderstanding, Jesus' example is our guide. He teaches us that even in our hardest moments we can choose to trust God's plan, and respond to the challenge with silence and faith. Such an attitude is not weakness but deep strength, born of unconditional trust in God.
q: When you face misunderstanding or blame, are you able to choose silence as Jesus did, and entrust everything to God? In such moments, how can you lean more deeply on his strength?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus as our example, so that we may learn to trust your will in hard times. Help us, when we face challenges and accusations, to respond with silence and faith, and to rely on your strength to get through. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now at the feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whom they asked of him.
There was one called Barabbas, bound with his fellow insurgents, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.
The multitude, crying aloud, began to ask him to do as he always did for them.
Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
For he perceived that for envy the chief priests had delivered him up.
But the chief priests stirred up the multitude, that he should release Barabbas to them instead.
Pilate again asked them, “What then should I do to him whom you call the King of the Jews?”
They cried out again, “Crucify him!”
Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has he done?” But they cried out exceedingly, “Crucify him!”
Pilate, wishing to please the multitude, released Barabbas to them, and handed over Jesus, when he had flogged him, to be crucified.
b: This passage describes the final verdict on Jesus before Pilate. Each Passover, Pilate customarily released one prisoner to please the Jewish crowd. But this time the choice became a contest between justice and injustice. Barabbas was a criminal who had taken part in an insurrection and murder, yet stirred up by the chief priests, the crowd chose to free this criminal and push the innocent Jesus toward death. Pilate knew the chief priests were motivated by envy, yet he gave in to the crowd's demand and handed Jesus over to be crucified.

This passage deeply reflects human weakness and sin. The crowd, incited, chose an unjust outcome, while Pilate, afraid of losing his power and influence, finally compromised and abandoned the justice a judge ought to uphold. Throughout it all Jesus remained silent and submissive, showing his complete trust in God's will.

This passage reminds us that even under great pressure and in the face of injustice, we should keep trusting God's will and not be shaken by circumstances. We are also called to reflect on whether our choices come from a love of justice, or whether we are yielding to outside pressure and human weakness.
q: When you face injustice or outside pressure, are you able to stand for righteousness and trust God's plan? Have you ever given in to human weakness and made a wrong choice?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us through Jesus' experience that even in injustice and pressure we must keep trusting your will. Give us wisdom and courage to stand firm in life's decisions and not yield to the pressure of our circumstances. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: The soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Praetorium; and they called together the whole cohort.
They clothed him with purple, and weaving a crown of thorns, they put it on him.
They began to salute him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They struck his head with a reed, and spat on him, and bowing their knees, did homage to him.
When they had mocked him, they took the purple off him, and put his own garments on him. They led him out to crucify him.
b: This passage records the humiliation and abuse Jesus suffered after he was sentenced to death. The Roman soldiers led Jesus into the courtyard of the governor's palace and called together the whole company of soldiers to mock him. They dressed him in a purple robe, the color of royalty, twisted a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and pretended to honor him, calling him "King of the Jews." They not only ridiculed him but struck his head with a reed and spat on him. These acts were deeply degrading and show the ugliness of human sin.

Through this humiliation Jesus bore it all in silence, showing his complete submission to God's will. As the Savior of the world, he was willing to endure such great suffering for us, and words cannot describe this love and sacrifice. This passage lets us see Jesus' suffering, and it also makes us reflect on human cruelty and on how we treat him.

This passage reminds us that Jesus' suffering was not only to redeem us from our sins but also to expose the evil deep within the human heart. As we meditate on his suffering, we should ask whether we sometimes treat Jesus' love and sacrifice as the soldiers did, with contempt and mockery. We are called to honor him, to give thanks for all he has done for us, and to answer his love with our lives.
q: Jesus bore such enormous humiliation and pain for us. Have we ever neglected or made light of his love? How can we better respond to Jesus' sacrifice and love in our daily lives?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see the suffering and shame Jesus bore for us. Help us to understand deeply the greatness of this love and to respond to his sacrifice with reverence and gratitude. May we remember Jesus' suffering often in our lives and show our love for him by our actions. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: They compelled one passing by, coming from the country, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go with them, that he might bear his cross.
They brought him to the place called Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, “The place of a skull.”
They offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he didn’t take it.
Crucifying him, they parted his garments among them, casting lots on them, what each should take.
It was the third hour,  and they crucified him.
The superscription of his accusation was written over him, “THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
b: This passage describes Jesus' road to Golgotha and his crucifixion. On the way, carrying his cross, Jesus was already extremely weak from the scourging and torture and could not carry the cross himself. So the Roman soldiers forced Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, to help carry it. This scene shows Jesus' human frailty and also highlights his love, which emptied itself completely.

When Jesus was brought to Golgotha (the place of the Skull), the soldiers offered him wine mixed with myrrh. This drink was usually given to dull the pain of the condemned, but Jesus refused it. He chose to bear the full suffering of the cross, which shows his obedience and sacrifice. Then Jesus was nailed to the cross, the cruelest punishment the Romans reserved for the worst criminals. The inscription above read "The King of the Jews," which was meant as mockery of Jesus' true identity and a distortion of his mission.

This passage reminds us that Jesus bore great pain and shame for us, and that his sacrifice is the highest expression of unconditional love. We are called to meditate on this love and receive his salvation with grateful hearts. We should also examine our own lives: are we willing to take up our own cross and follow in Jesus' footsteps?
q: Jesus carried the cross for us. Are we willing to take up our own cross in daily life and follow in his footsteps? How can we show such love and sacrifice in our everyday lives?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, who carried the cross for us and bore the suffering we deserved. Help us to take up our own cross courageously and follow in Jesus' footsteps, living out his love and sacrifice. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: With him they crucified two robbers; one on his right hand, and one on his left.
The Scripture was fulfilled, which says, “He was counted with transgressors.”
Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads, and saying, “Ha! You who destroy the temple, and build it in three days,
save yourself, and come down from the cross!”
Likewise, also the chief priests mocking among themselves with the scribes said, “He saved others. He can’t save himself.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe him.”  Those who were crucified with him also insulted him.
b: This passage records the mockery and humiliation Jesus suffered on the cross. When he was crucified, two robbers were crucified with him, one on each side, fulfilling the prophecy that he would be counted among the transgressors. Passersby, the chief priests and the scribes all seized the chance to ridicule him, and even the criminals crucified with him did the same. They jeered, "You who destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself and come down from the cross!" Their taunts were full of scorn and contempt, as if a man who could not save himself could hardly be called the King of Israel and the Christ.

This passage shows that, even in the face of the worst human sin, Jesus held to his mission and did not answer the provocation and mockery. He bore it all in silence in order to complete God's plan of redemption. Jesus' silence and submission are the greatest proof of his love and sacrifice for us. He was not shaken by the humiliation but went on to finish his mission with even greater resolve.

This passage reminds us that Jesus' cross was not because of weakness, but was the greatest sacrifice he made to redeem us. We should look at his cross with gratitude and reverence, for it is the fullest expression of his love for us. When we meet difficulties and challenges in life, we should also learn from Jesus' example, keep trusting God's will, and not be shaken by the voices around us.
q: When we meet hardship and ridicule in life, can we, like Jesus, keep trusting God's will? How can we understand more deeply, and respond to, the love and sacrifice Jesus showed on the cross?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see the shame and suffering Jesus bore on the cross. Help us also to keep trusting your will and not be shaken by hardship and ridicule. May we take Jesus' love and sacrifice as our example and take up our cross with courage. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When the sixth hour  had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” which is, being interpreted, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
Some of those who stood by, when they heard it, said, “Behold, he is calling Elijah.”
One ran, and filling a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink, saying, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and gave up the spirit.
The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.
When the centurion, who stood by opposite him, saw that he cried out like this and breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
b: This passage records Jesus' final moments on the cross and the deep suffering he went through. From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness came over the whole land, symbolizing the spiritual darkness the whole world went through at that moment. In his hour of greatest anguish, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" This is the fullest expression of Jesus bearing the sins of all humanity: he experienced a brief separation from the Father, and that separation was for our redemption.

At the moment Jesus breathed his last, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, symbolizing that through Jesus' sacrifice the barrier between God and humanity has been broken. We no longer need to approach the Most Holy Place through priests, because Jesus has become our mediator with God, and his death has brought us a new relationship with God. The centurion's declaration, "Truly this man was the Son of God!" is also a final confirmation of Jesus' identity, showing that his death had divine meaning.

This passage lets us reflect on the suffering and sacrifice Jesus bore on the cross. His death opened a new relationship with God for us, so that we can come before God boldly and without fear. We should remember Jesus' suffering often with grateful hearts, and live out the truth of this salvation in our daily lives.
q: Jesus' suffering has given us a new relationship with God. Do we give thanks for this salvation and respond to it in our daily lives? How can we experience and live out more deeply the spiritual freedom this salvation brings?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you that through the suffering and death of Jesus Christ you have opened the way for us to have fellowship with you. Help us to remember this salvation often and to respond to Jesus' sacrifice with gratitude. May our lives reveal your glory and live out a genuine faith. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: There were also women watching from afar, among whom were both Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
who, when he was in Galilee, followed him and served him; and many other women who came up with him to Jerusalem.
b: This passage mentions the women who watched from a distance as Jesus suffered. They included Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome. They had faithfully followed Jesus and served him in his ministry. Their presence shows that at the moment Jesus was crucified, although most of the disciples had scattered, these women were still there, displaying their courage and loyalty.

These women played an important role in Jesus' ministry. They not only followed and served him during his life but also kept faithful company with him in his suffering, a testimony to their faith and love. Their example reminds us that true faith is not following when things go well, but holding firm when times are hard.

This passage encourages us to keep following Jesus steadfastly through difficulties and challenges. Whatever changes our circumstances bring, we should be like these women, remaining loyal and loving toward the Lord and serving him in practical ways.
q: When we face difficulties and challenges, do we still follow Jesus steadfastly? How can we practice such loyalty and love in our daily lives?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see the example of these women who faithfully followed Jesus. Give us courage and strength to keep following you faithfully in life's adversity and to show our love for you in practical ways. May our faith grow stronger in hard times and bring glory to your name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When evening had now come, because it was the Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member who also himself was looking for God’s Kingdom, came. He boldly went in to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.
Pilate marveled if he were already dead; and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether he had been dead long.
When he found out from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
He bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb which had been cut out of a rock. He rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, saw where he was laid.
b: This passage records the burial of Jesus. Joseph of Arimathea was a respected member of the council who was himself waiting for the kingdom of God. He boldly asked Pilate for Jesus' body, which shows his deep respect and love for Jesus. When Pilate learned that Jesus was already dead, he allowed Joseph to take the body. Joseph bought a linen cloth, wrapped Jesus' body in it, and laid him in a new tomb.

This passage highlights Joseph's courage and faith. He was willing to risk openly declaring his faith after Jesus' death, an act that shows his love and admiration for Jesus. Joseph's action shows that true faith needs courage at the critical moment, and does not fear the risks that come with standing for it.

This passage encourages us on the path of faith to have the courage to stand up and declare our loyalty to Christ. Whatever our circumstances, we should witness for the Lord with faith and courage and put our faith into practice in our lives.
q: When we face challenges to our faith, can we, like Joseph of Arimathea, boldly declare our loyalty to Jesus? How can we practice such courage and faith in our daily lives?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us through the example of Joseph of Arimathea how to show courage and loyalty in our faith. Give us strength not to fear risk in our lives and to bear bold witness for Christ. May we follow you without wavering in hard times and honor your name by our actions. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, bought spices, that they might come and anoint him.
Very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
They were saying among themselves, “Who will roll away the stone from the door of the tomb for us?”
for it was very big. Looking up, they saw that the stone was rolled back.
Entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe, and they were amazed.
He said to them, “Don’t be amazed. You seek Jesus, the Nazarene, who has been crucified. He has risen. He is not here. Behold, the place where they laid him!
But go, tell his disciples and Peter, ‘He goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him, as he said to you.’ ”
They went out, and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had come on them. They said nothing to anyone; for they were afraid.
b: This passage describes the resurrection of Jesus, the heart of the Christian faith. Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome went to Jesus' tomb after the Sabbath, hoping to anoint his body with spices. But they found that the stone had been rolled away, and they saw a young man dressed in a white robe, who told them that Jesus had risen and was not in the tomb. The news filled them with fear and amazement, for they realized that what they had witnessed was an utterly holy event.

This passage underscores the great significance of Jesus' resurrection. The resurrection not only proves Jesus' deity but also confirms his power over death, which is the foundation of our faith. The young man's message told them to go and tell the disciples and Peter that Jesus had risen and would meet them in Galilee. This instruction shows how important the resurrection is: it is not only a miracle, but a message of salvation that must be proclaimed far and wide.

This passage reminds us that Jesus' resurrection is the cornerstone of our faith. Whatever challenges or fears we face, we should believe that Jesus has conquered death and is our hope of eternal life. Like those women, we should boldly proclaim this good news and live out this faith in our lives.
q: Jesus' resurrection gives us hope of eternal life. How can we live out this faith in our daily lives and boldly share this good news with others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you that through the resurrection of Jesus Christ you have given us hope of eternal life. Give us courage to witness to this great salvation in our lives, and to follow Jesus with firm faith, unafraid of any challenge. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now when he had risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
She went and told those who had been with him, as they mourned and wept.
When they heard that he was alive, and had been seen by her, they disbelieved.
b: This passage describes how, after his resurrection, Jesus first appeared to Mary Magdalene. Jesus had once cast seven demons out of Mary, which shows his saving power in her life. Mary witnessed Jesus' resurrection and immediately went to tell those who had followed Jesus, but because of their grief and unbelief, they could not accept the news right away.

This passage highlights the difficulty the first witnesses to the resurrection met: even Jesus' closest followers were confused and unbelieving when they heard this astonishing news. Yet this takes nothing away from the reality of the resurrection; rather, it lets us see human weakness and the testing of faith.

This passage reminds us that faith is vital when we face difficulties and challenges. We should trust what God has done, even when people around us do not understand or doubt. We are called to share our testimony of faith, and even if our testimony meets doubt or unbelief, we should keep on proclaiming what God has done.
q: When our faith is met with doubt or unbelief, how can we hold firm in faith and boldly bear witness to Jesus' salvation and resurrection?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you that through Jesus' resurrection you have given us hope of eternal life. Help us hold firm in faith, and to boldly witness to Jesus' resurrection even in the face of unbelief and doubt. May our lives be a testimony to your salvation and draw more people to you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: After these things he was revealed in another form to two of them, as they walked, on their way into the country.
They went away and told it to the rest. They didn’t believe them, either.
b: This passage records another appearance of Jesus to his disciples after his resurrection. This time he appeared in a different form, so that two disciples walking into the country did not recognize him. This change points to the risen Jesus, whose existence goes beyond what the eye can see and shows the full revelation of his divine nature. These two disciples witnessed Jesus' resurrection, but when they went back and told the rest of the disciples, they were met with unbelief.

This passage underscores the challenge of resurrection faith: even when people witness a miracle with their own eyes, unbelief can remain. The disciples' doubt reflects the common human reaction to supernatural events. It reminds us that faith is a spiritual reception that goes beyond reason and sight, and it takes the Holy Spirit's leading and revelation to truly receive what God has done.

This passage reminds us that faith does not rely only on what we see and hear, but on understanding deep in the heart and on the Holy Spirit's guidance. On the path of faith we need to keep seeking God's revelation and to keep proclaiming this message of salvation, holding on to our faith even when we are doubted.
q: When we face doubt and questioning about our faith, how can we rely on the Holy Spirit to hold firm in faith and proclaim the salvation of Jesus Christ to others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for continually revealing your truth and grace in our lives. Help us, when we face unbelief and doubt, to hold on to our faith and to rely on the Holy Spirit's leading to know and receive the salvation of Jesus Christ. May our lives be vessels that bear witness to your truth and power. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Afterward he was revealed to the eleven themselves as they sat at the table, and he rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they didn’t believe those who had seen him after he had risen.
He said to them, “Go into all the world, and preach the Good News to the whole creation.
b: This passage describes how, after his resurrection, Jesus appeared to the eleven disciples and rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart. Although Jesus had risen and witnesses had come to tell them the news, the disciples remained hard-hearted and unwilling to believe the miracle had happened. Jesus' rebuke reminds us that faith is more than hearing and seeing; it also requires our hearts to receive and obey.

In this passage Jesus gives the disciples an important mission: to go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature. This is not only a command to the disciples but a call to every believer who follows Jesus. We are called to share the gospel and pass on the message of salvation to everyone, whatever their background. This is our important mission in the world.

This passage makes us ask: do we sometimes miss what God is doing because of doubt or a hard heart? Have we faithfully answered Jesus' call and actively proclaimed the gospel? May we, when we face challenges to our faith, hold on to our faith and answer Jesus' Great Commission with action.
q: When we face questions in our faith, do we still hold firm in faith? How can we put Jesus' Great Commission into practice in daily life and share the gospel with others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for giving us the mission of proclaiming the gospel. Help us no longer to doubt in our faith but to answer your call with firm faith. May our lives bear witness to your love and power and share this message of salvation with more people. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who disbelieves will be condemned.
These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new languages;
they will take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it will in no way hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.”
b: This passage tells of the promise Jesus gave his disciples: whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned. Jesus stressed the necessity of faith and told the disciples that true faith brings signs that follow, which become the mark and testimony of believers.

The signs Jesus mentioned, including casting out demons, speaking in new languages, picking up serpents without harm, drinking poison without being hurt, and laying hands on the sick to heal them, are all displays of God's power, given to confirm the truth and authority of the gospel. These signs show the power of faith and God's protection of believers, enabling them to overcome in difficulties and challenges.

This passage shows us that faith is not merely knowledge in the mind but needs to be practiced and experienced. When we answer God's call in faith, our lives will experience God's wonderful works, which are not only blessings to us but also a testimony to those around us. We are called to live out such faith, so that signs and God's grace are continually shown in our lives.
q: Do we believe and expect God to work miracles in our lives? How can we live out our faith so that God's works become a testimony, and a source of strength, for us and for others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for the promises you give us in faith, so that we may overcome under your protection and grace. Help us live out your truth in faith, and let your signs and power be shown in our lives as a testimony to all. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: So then the Lord, after he had spoken to them, was received up into heaven, and sat down at the right hand of God.
They went out, and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word by the signs that followed. Amen.
b: This passage records that after Jesus had given the disciples the Great Commission, he was taken up into heaven and sat at the right hand of God. Jesus' ascension marked the complete end of his earthly ministry, and it also proclaimed that he is in heaven with the Father, interceding for us and reigning as King. Jesus' ascension let the disciples understand that they had now been entrusted with the mission of proclaiming the gospel, and that Jesus would work with them, confirming the message with signs that followed.

The disciples faithfully carried out this mission. They went out and preached everywhere, and signs followed them, which became a powerful testimony to the truth of the gospel. Although Jesus ascended, his Spirit remains with the disciples and continues to work signs and wonders on earth, so that more people may come to faith.

This passage reminds us that Jesus' ascension does not mean he is separated from us; rather, he is with us from heaven and continues to work in our lives through the Holy Spirit. We are called, like the disciples, to proclaim the gospel faithfully and to expect God to do great things through our service. Wherever we are, Jesus works with us, and our faith and actions will bear witness to his reality.
q: How do we fulfill the mission of proclaiming the gospel in our daily lives? Do we expect and rely on God working with us, so that the truth of the gospel is shown around us?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you that through the ascension of Jesus Christ we know he is with us, and that you give us strength to proclaim the gospel. Help us faithfully fulfill your mission in our lives and expect your signs to follow our actions as a testimony to the gospel. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Since many have undertaken to set in order a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us,
even as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word delivered them to us,
it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus;
that you might know the certainty concerning the things in which you were instructed.
b: This passage is the preface to the Gospel of Luke, in which Luke explains to his excellency Theophilus the purpose and method of his writing. Luke stresses that what he records rests on careful investigation and on the accounts of eyewitnesses, which assures the truth and reliability of his narrative. He hopes that Theophilus, and all who read this Gospel, may have firm confidence in what they have been taught, because all of it is certain and trustworthy.

From this preface we see Luke's careful attitude toward recording the work of the gospel. He relied not only on his own investigation but also on the accounts of those who had been eyewitnesses of Jesus' ministry from the beginning, to ensure the truth and accuracy of the gospel. This teaches us that in seeking the truth of our faith we too should examine carefully and hold fast to the truth, so that our faith is built on a solid foundation.

This passage reminds us that the foundation of faith must be built on sure truth. We should treasure the truth of Scripture that God has revealed, and hold to it and practice it in our lives. Luke wrote so that Theophilus might be certain of what he had been taught, and he encourages us, on the path of faith, to pursue the truth with the same zeal and care and to bear witness to God's truth in our lives.
q: In your life of faith, do you diligently study and examine the truth of Scripture? How do you make sure your faith rests on a solid and certain foundation?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you that through Luke's Gospel we may come to know the work and truth of Jesus Christ. Give us wisdom and a humble heart, so that we may study your word diligently and put this truth into practice in our lives. May our faith be built on a sure foundation, and may your truth and love be shown in our lives every day. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the priestly division of Abijah. He had a wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
They were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.
But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and they both were well advanced in years.
b: This passage introduces Zechariah and Elizabeth, a godly couple who were both righteous before God and walked blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord. Yet this couple faced the hardship of being unable to have children, which in the culture of that time was regarded as a disgrace. Although their lives were blameless before God, they still went through such a trial.

The story of Zechariah and Elizabeth reminds us that the righteous are not exempt from trials and difficulties in this world. Even if we keep God's commandments, we may meet all kinds of challenges and hardships. But as this passage shows, in facing this difficulty they still held firm in trusting God, which shows the depth of their faith and their dependence on God.

Through this passage God tells us that whatever trials we face in life, as long as we walk righteously before him and keep his commandments, God will step in at the right time and accomplish everything according to his good pleasure. We should face life's challenges in faith, believing that God's plan and timing are the best.
q: In your life right now, what trials leave you confused or discouraged? How can you keep your faith in God through these trials and rely on his strength to pass through them?
