pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us through the story of Zechariah and Elizabeth how to keep faith in trials. Give us strength to keep trusting you in difficulty and to see your wonderful works in your own time. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his division
according to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to enter into the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
The whole multitude of the people were praying outside at the hour of incense.
An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
Zacharias was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
But the angel said to him, “Don’t be afraid, Zacharias, because your request has been heard. Your wife, Elizabeth, will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great in the sight of the Lord, and he will drink no wine nor strong drink. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb.
He will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God.

He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, ‘to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children,’ and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to prepare a people prepared for the Lord.”
b: This passage records the angel appearing to Zechariah and foretelling that his wife Elizabeth would bear a son, who would become the forerunner of the Lord. Zechariah had entered the temple to burn incense in the course of his priestly duty, and there the angel appeared to him and told him that God had heard his prayer. The angel announced John's birth and his mission: he would be great before the Lord and would turn many to God.

This passage lets us see that God's plan for our lives often goes beyond our understanding. Zechariah and Elizabeth had long been unable to have children, yet God chose to give them in their old age a child with a special mission. This reminds us that however impossible our situation may look, God has his time and his plan, and his plan goes far beyond what we can imagine.

This passage also stresses the importance of prayer. Zechariah's prayer was heard, which shows his trust in God. Even after years of childlessness he kept on praying, which is an expression of deep faith. We too should rely on God in prayer, believing that he will accomplish his purpose in his own time.
q: What unanswered prayers do you have in your life? How can you keep your faith in God while you wait, believing that his plan and timing are the best?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see that your plan goes far beyond our understanding. Help us keep trusting you in prayer, whatever difficulties or challenges we face. May our hearts always rest on your faithfulness. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Zacharias said to the angel, “How can I be sure of this? For I am an old man, and my wife is well advanced in years.”
The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
Behold, you will be silent and not able to speak until the day that these things will happen, because you didn’t believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their proper time.”
The people were waiting for Zacharias, and they marveled that he delayed in the temple.
When he came out, he could not speak to them. They perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple. He continued making signs to them, and remained mute.
When the days of his service were fulfilled, he departed to his house.
After these days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she hid herself five months, saying,
“Thus has the Lord done to me in the days in which he looked at me, to take away my reproach among men.”
b: This passage describes Zechariah's doubt about the angel's prophecy and the punishment of muteness he received because of it. Zechariah doubted God's promise because of his age, but the angel Gabriel reminded him that God's word will surely be fulfilled. Although Zechariah was made mute because of his unbelief, God's plan did not change. In the end God fulfilled his promise, Elizabeth conceived, and this brought great joy and removed the disgrace of her childlessness through the years.

This passage reminds us that when we face God's promises, we should respond in faith and not be limited by the difficulties in front of us. Zechariah's experience tells us that God's plan does not change because of our doubt, yet a lack of faith may keep us from seeing God's blessing right away. God's faithfulness never changes; our responsibility is to trust and obey his will.

This passage also shows how God turns disgrace into glory. Elizabeth's long childlessness was regarded as shameful in that time, but God finally gave her the grace of conceiving and made her a witness of his blessing. When we face disgrace and hardship in life, we should believe in God's power and purpose: he can turn every difficulty into an opportunity to testify to his glory.
q: Have you ever regretted doubting God's promise? How can you keep faith in God's promises in future challenges and see his work?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for giving us an example of faith. Help us, when we face difficulties, not to be troubled by present limits but to rely wholeheartedly on your promises and faithfulness. May our lives be vessels that testify to your glory. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now in the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth,
to a virgin pledged to be married to a man whose name was Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
Having come in, the angel said to her, “Rejoice, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women!”
But when she saw him, she was greatly troubled at the saying, and considered what kind of salutation this might be.
The angel said to her, “Don’t be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
Behold, you will conceive in your womb and give birth to a son, and shall name him ‘Jesus.’
He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,
and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. There will be no end to his Kingdom.”
Mary said to the angel, “How can this be, seeing I am a virgin?”
The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore also the holy one who is born from you will be called the Son of God.
Behold, Elizabeth your relative also has conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month with her who was called barren.
For nothing spoken by God is impossible.”
Mary said, “Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.” The angel departed from her.
b: This passage records the angel Gabriel announcing to Mary that she would become the mother of Jesus. Mary was troubled by the angel's greeting, but Gabriel told her that she had found favor with God. Although Mary was perplexed because she was not yet married, the angel explained that this would be the work of the Holy Spirit and stressed that "nothing spoken by God is without power." In the end Mary responded in faith and submission, accepting the call to become the mother of the Savior.

This passage shows the humility and submission Mary displayed when she faced God's call. Although it was a task hard to understand and accept, she did not refuse, but answered, "Behold, the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word." This is the highest expression of faith and submission: she fully trusted God's will and power, and she sets an example for each of us.

This passage also stresses that God's power goes beyond all the laws of nature. Mary's conception was the work of the Holy Spirit, revealing God's limitless power. This reminds us that when God's plan unfolds in our lives, we should not limit his work by human understanding, but trust his great power and believe that his purpose will surely be fulfilled.
q: When God calls you, are you willing, like Mary, to submit fully and trust his plan?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see Mary's faith and submission. Help us, when we face the callings and challenges of life, to answer you with the same faith, to submit to your will, and to believe that your great power will accomplish everything. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Mary arose in those days and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah,
and entered into the house of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She called out with a loud voice and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
Why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For behold, when the voice of your greeting came into my ears, the baby leaped in my womb for joy!
Blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of the things which have been spoken to her from the Lord!”
b: This passage describes Mary visiting her relative Elizabeth. When these two women, both blessed by God, met, the baby in Elizabeth's womb (later John the Baptist) leaped inside her, showing his welcome of the Savior in Mary's womb. Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and called Mary a blessed woman, declaring that the child she carried was blessed, because she had believed that what God had spoken would be fulfilled.

This passage stresses the blessing of faith. Elizabeth called Mary blessed because she believed God's word. This kind of faith does not rely on sight but wholly on God's promise. Mary's faith is an example to each of us, teaching us how to trust God's word in daily life even when we have not yet seen the promise fulfilled.

This passage also shows how God works in our lives through the Holy Spirit. The baby in Elizabeth's womb leaped at Mary's arrival, showing the Holy Spirit's sovereignty in this holy meeting. We should expect and welcome the Holy Spirit's guidance in our lives; he enables us to see God's works, fills our hearts, and gives us heavenly joy and peace.
q: Have you experienced the Holy Spirit's guidance and filling in your life? How can you trust God's word more deeply and live by faith?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see the faith and joy of Mary and Elizabeth. Help us also to trust you this way and to find peace and joy in your promised word. May our hearts be often filled with the Holy Spirit, and may we share this blessing with others in your love. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord.
My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
for he has looked at the humble state of his servant. For behold, from now on, all generations will call me blessed.
For he who is mighty has done great things for me. Holy is his name.
His mercy is for generations of generations on those who fear him.
He has shown strength with his arm. He has scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.
He has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly.
He has filled the hungry with good things. He has sent the rich away empty.
He has given help to Israel, his servant, that he might remember mercy,
as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring forever.”
Mary stayed with her about three months, and then returned to her house.
b: This passage records Mary's song of praise. Having felt God's grace and mercy, she praised and thanked him from the bottom of her heart. Her song celebrates God's great works and affirms his personal care for her and his saving of her. Mary's song also reflects God's love for all humanity, especially his mercy toward the lowly and his lifting them up.

Mary's song teaches us how to express gratitude and reverence in our faith. She praised God not only for the grace she herself had received, but also for what he has done throughout history. This reminds us that in every season of life, whether easy or hard, we should worship God with thankful hearts, because his love and mercy never change.

This passage also shows us God's love and blessing for the humble. Mary was a lowly servant girl, yet God chose her to carry out the great plan of salvation. This tells us that in God's eyes, a humble and reverent heart is worth more than worldly power and wealth. When we humble ourselves and depend on God, he gives grace and accomplishes wonderful things in our lives.
q: In your life, do you worship God with a thankful and humble heart? How can you put this attitude of faith into practice every day?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us through Mary's song how to worship you with gratitude and reverence. Help us, in every season of life, to recognize your grace and mercy and to depend on you with humble hearts. May our lives be a testimony to your wonderful works and bring glory to your name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now the time that Elizabeth should give birth was fulfilled, and she gave birth to a son.
Her neighbors and her relatives heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day, they came to circumcise the child; and they would have called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
His mother answered, “Not so; but he will be called John.”
They said to her, “There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.”
They made signs to his father, what he would have him called.
He asked for a writing tablet, and wrote, “His name is John.” They all marveled.
His mouth was opened immediately and his tongue freed, and he spoke, blessing God.
Fear came on all who lived around them, and all these sayings were talked about throughout all the hill country of Judea.
All who heard them laid them up in their heart, saying, “What then will this child be?” The hand of the Lord was with him.
b: This passage records the birth and naming of John the Baptist, and the miracle of God opening the mouth of Zechariah, who had been struck mute for his unbelief, so that he could praise God again. When John was born, everyone expected him to be named after his father, Zechariah, as tradition required, but Elizabeth and Zechariah insisted on following the angel's instruction and named the child John. This act showed their obedience to God's will and bore witness to God's work.

After experiencing God's discipline, Zechariah was able to speak again, a sign that his faith had been restored. This miracle deeply stirred those around them and set people wondering what this child would become. The passage stresses the importance of obeying God's will and reminds us that God's plans often go beyond our expectations and traditions.

This passage also reveals God's mercy and faithfulness. That Elizabeth and Zechariah had a son in their old age was God's answer to their prayers of many years. Even though Zechariah had for a time lost his speech through doubt, when he obeyed, God still showed his mercy and restored his voice. This encourages us, when we face God's call, not to doubt but to trust fully and obey his will.
q: When you face life's decisions, are you willing to obey God's will, whether or not it fits your expectations or tradition?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us, through the birth and naming of John the Baptist, how important it is to obey your will. Help us, when we face choices in life, to answer your call with faith and obedience, and to bear witness to your wonderful works. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: His father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit, and prophesied, saying,
“Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, for he has visited and redeemed his people;
and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David
(as he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets who have been from of old),
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us;
to show mercy toward our fathers, to remember his holy covenant,
the oath which he swore to Abraham our father,
to grant to us that we, being delivered out of the hand of our enemies, should serve him without fear,
in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give knowledge of salvation to his people by the remission of their sins,
because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
to shine on those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death; to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
The child was growing and becoming strong in spirit, and was in the desert until the day of his public appearance to Israel.
b: This passage records Zechariah's praise and prophecy to God as he was filled with the Holy Spirit. He praised God for the redemption he has accomplished and looked back on God's promises to Israel throughout history. He prophesied especially about the mission of his son John, who as a prophet of the Most High would prepare the way of the Lord and lead the people to know salvation. Zechariah's prophecy is full of gratitude and a deep understanding of God's plan, showing his faith in God and his obedience.

Zechariah's song reflects his understanding of God's plan of redemption and his confidence in God's promises. He recognized that God was fulfilling these promises through his son John and through Jesus Christ, which is the hope not only of the nation of Israel but of salvation for all humanity. As we read this passage, we should learn from Zechariah's faith and praise God with grateful hearts, because his plan has been faithful and unchanging from ancient times until now.

This passage also reminds us that God's promises can be trusted and that he has a special plan for each of our lives. Just as Zechariah prophesied that John would be the prophet who prepares the way of the Lord, each of us has a mission of our own, and these missions have been prepared by God beforehand. We should seek God's leading in prayer and devotion, so that we may fulfill his will in our own lives.
q: Are you seeking God's plan and will for your life? How can you better understand and obey God's calling on your life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us, through Zechariah's song, how wonderful your promises and plans are. Help us in our daily lives to hold on to faith and to seek your will, so that our lives may be a testimony to your glory. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now in those days, a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled.
This was the first enrollment made when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
All went to enroll themselves, everyone to his own city.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to David’s city, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David;
to enroll himself with Mary, who was pledged to be married to him as wife, being pregnant.
While they were there, the day had come for her to give birth.
She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
b: This passage describes the birth of Jesus, one of the most important events in all the Gospels. By the decree of Caesar Augustus, Joseph and Mary went to Bethlehem, and against this historical background Jesus was born in a manger. What a humble beginning! God chose to give his Son in such simple surroundings. This shows his humility and lets us see that God's salvation makes no distinction between rich and poor or high and low; his love is for everyone.

Through the obedience of Mary and Joseph, Jesus was born in Bethlehem, fulfilling the prophecies of the Old Testament. This reminds us that no matter how ordinary or unbelievable God's plan may seem, it will in the end be accomplished according to his will. We should learn from Mary and Joseph's obedience: whatever the circumstances, we trust and follow God's leading, and he will fulfill his plan at the right time.

This passage also shows us how special the birth of Jesus was. Even in the humblest of places, his coming brought immeasurable light and hope. This teaches us that whatever our situation, we should welcome Jesus and let him into our lives, because his coming brings true peace and joy.
q: In your life, are you willing to make room for Jesus and let him be the Lord of your life? How can you express such obedience and faith in your daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for sending Jesus into the world, born in humility to bring us salvation. Help us to learn from the obedience of Mary and Joseph, and to prepare a place in our hearts for Jesus, so that he may be the Lord of our lives. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.
For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”
Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God, and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.”
When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
They came with haste, and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.
When they saw it, they publicized widely the saying which was spoken to them about this child.
All who heard it wondered at the things which were spoken to them by the shepherds.
But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.
b: This passage records the scene of the angels announcing the good news to the shepherds at the birth of Jesus. Shepherds were people of low standing in society, yet God chose to tell them first the good news of salvation. This shows that God's love makes no distinction between rich and poor or noble and lowly. The angel announced the good news to the shepherds and led them to find Jesus, as part of God's revealing his salvation to humankind.

After hearing the angels' message, the shepherds hurried off to find Jesus and spread the word about what they had seen and heard. They became the first messengers of the gospel, which reminds us that when we receive God's grace and the gospel, we too should be eager to share it with others. The shepherds returned glorifying God for all they had seen and heard, teaching us that in daily life, in matters great and small, we should give the glory to God, because every good thing comes from him.

Mary, for her part, kept all these things in her heart and pondered them. This shows her deep sensitivity to what God was doing and her spiritual maturity. We too should learn from Mary: when we experience God's grace and work, we should not only give thanks but also reflect and meditate, letting these experiences take root in our hearts and become strength for our faith.
q: When you receive God's grace, do you share it with others right away? How can you keep reflecting on God's works and giving thanks in your daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for sending the good news of Jesus' birth to the shepherds through the angels, and for letting us see that your salvation makes no distinction between high and low. Help us to share this good news eagerly in our lives and to give you the glory in everything. May our hearts keep thinking on your works and be made firm in faith. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When eight days were fulfilled for the circumcision of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
When the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him up to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord
(as it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”),
and to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, “A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.”
b: In this passage, Mary and Joseph, following the Law of Moses, had Jesus circumcised and brought him to the temple to present the offering. They offered a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, the offering the Law prescribed for poor families. This shows the humble background of Jesus' family, and also their faithfulness to God's law and their reverence for him. All these actions show us that Jesus did not come in the image of wealth or power, but accomplished God's plan of salvation in humility and obedience.

The obedience Mary and Joseph showed in these actions teaches us that, whatever our circumstances, we should follow God's will and commands. Their obedience was not merely outward form; it came from reverence and love for God in their hearts. Their obedience also meant that Jesus began his work of redemption in human history in the humblest way, foreshadowing how he would fulfill his mission on earth through perfect obedience to the Father's will.

In addition, this passage stresses the importance of regularity and ritual in the life of faith. Even though Jesus was the Son of God, Mary and Joseph still kept the law and carried out the rites of circumcision and offering. This reminds us that rites and observances play an important part in the life of faith. They help us stay focused on God and put our faith into practice in daily life.
q: In your life, do you take part regularly in the practices and rites of your faith? How can you express obedience to and reverence for God through them?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us, through the obedience of Mary and Joseph, how to follow your will in daily life. Help us, in whatever circumstances, to serve you with humble and obedient hearts, and to follow your law even in the smallest things. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, looking for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.
It had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
He came in the Spirit into the temple. When the parents brought in the child, Jesus, that they might do concerning him according to the custom of the law,
then he received him into his arms, and blessed God, and said,
“Now you are releasing your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace;
for my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared before the face of all peoples;
a light for revelation to the nations, and the glory of your people Israel.”
b: This passage describes Simeon, a righteous and devout old man who had been waiting for the coming of Israel's Redeemer. The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would see the Christ before he died. When he saw Jesus, Simeon was deeply moved and recognized that this was the salvation he had long awaited. His praise expressed his trust in God and his gratitude, because God had kept his promise and let him see the Savior with his own eyes in his lifetime.

Simeon's faith and hope set an example for us. He held firmly to God's promise and stayed patient and faithful through a long wait. This reminds us that God's promises will surely be fulfilled in his own time, and we need to wait with patience and faith, however hard the process may be. God's plan and timing are always perfect; we should trust his wisdom and keep seeking his guidance.

In addition, Simeon's prophecy reveals that Jesus' mission was not only to save Israel but also to be a light to the Gentiles. This helps us see that Jesus' salvation is prepared for all humanity, regardless of nation or people. As followers of Christ, we should also proclaim this good news to everyone, so that more people may come into the Lord's light and experience his salvation and glory.
q: While you wait for God's promises to be fulfilled, are you able to keep patience and faith? How can you keep following God faithfully during that time?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us through Simeon's faith to wait for and trust in your promises. Give us patience and faith, so that we do not lose heart while waiting for your promises, and so that we may be your witnesses in life, proclaiming your salvation to the world. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Joseph and his mother were marveling at the things which were spoken concerning him,
and Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary, his mother, “Behold, this child is set for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign which is spoken against.
Yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
b: This passage continues Simeon's prophecy. After blessing Jesus and his parents, he made a startling prophecy to Mary. Simeon prophesied that Jesus would be a sign for the falling and rising of many in Israel, meaning that Jesus' coming would cause division and challenge, that he would reveal the true thoughts of people's hearts and become a touchstone of faith. It also foretold that Jesus' mission would bring suffering, so much so that Mary herself would be pierced to the heart by what her son went through.

Simeon's prophecy shows us that following Jesus is not an easy road. The gospel of Jesus does bring salvation and hope, but it also challenges our values and way of life. Jesus' words and actions reveal the true nature of the human heart and make people face their real condition. This reminds us that, as we follow Christ, we need the courage to face these challenges and to be willing to bear the cost that may come for his sake.

In addition, Simeon's prophecy to Mary also helps us see that God's plan includes suffering and sacrifice. As Jesus' mother, Mary would witness his suffering and death with her own eyes, which foreshadowed that the way of the cross was the necessary way. This is also a reminder to us: the life of faith is not smooth sailing, and we may meet trials and pain, but these are part of God's plan, for the sake of a greater purpose and glory.
q: When your faith is challenged, are you willing to bear the cost of following Jesus? How can you remain faithful to God in difficulty?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us, through Simeon's prophecy, of the cost of following Jesus. Give us courage and strength, so that when we face challenges and difficulties we may still hold fast to our faith and depend on your guidance in all circumstances. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: There was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (she was of a great age, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
and she had been a widow for about eighty-four years), who didn’t depart from the temple, worshiping with fastings and petitions night and day.
Coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke of him to all those who were looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
b: This passage introduces the prophetess Anna, a devout woman who dedicated her whole life to serving in the temple. Anna's life was full of the witness of faith. After becoming a widow in her youth, she stayed in the temple for many years, fasting and praying, serving God night and day without ceasing. Her perseverance and faithfulness show her complete dependence on God and her love for him.

When Anna saw Jesus, she immediately recognized him as the Savior God had promised, and she announced this good news to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem. This shows her duty as a prophet and her deep understanding of and faith in God's plan. Anna's witness reminds us that, whatever our age or situation, we can be part of God's plan and testify to his faithfulness with our lives.

Anna's life is an encouragement to all believers: whatever difficulty or loss we have gone through, as long as we serve God faithfully, he will surely use us and make us part of his plan. Anna is not only an example of faith; she is also a reminder to us to wait patiently for God's promises and to serve faithfully while we wait, until we see them fulfilled.
q: In your life right now, how do you stay faithful and steadfast toward God? How can you keep your zeal for serving while you wait for God's promises?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us, through Anna's witness, to persevere and be faithful in our faith. Help us not to lose faith while we wait, and to be willing to serve you every day of our lives and be part of your plan. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When they had accomplished all things that were according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city, Nazareth.
The child was growing, and was becoming strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
b: This passage briefly describes Jesus' childhood growth. After Joseph and Mary had done everything required by the Law, they returned to Nazareth in Galilee, where Jesus grew up. This description shows Jesus' growth in his humanity: like us, he grew strong in body and increased in wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.

Jesus' growing up in Nazareth was a process of ordinary life, yet this takes nothing away from his divinity. On the contrary, it emphasizes the meaning of his becoming fully human, so that he can fully understand our weaknesses and challenges. This reminds us that God's grace is shown not only in supernatural ways in our lives but also continually in everyday life. We should seek God's wisdom and strength in every ordinary day and let his grace fill our lives.

In addition, this passage reminds us that however ordinary or plain our lives may look, we can experience God's grace and guidance in them. Jesus' childhood sets an example for us: he grew up in ordinary surroundings, yet was full of wisdom and the grace of God, and we should pursue this kind of growth in our own lives.
q: In your daily life, how do you seek God's wisdom and grace? How can you witness God's work in ordinary days?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see Jesus' growth in Nazareth, which reminds us that we can experience your grace in ordinary life. Give us wisdom and strength, so that in our daily lives we too may reflect your love and truth. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.
